content.comment_body: You can only connect pins that have the same type of connection. Here is an overview: Digital connections are represented as thin lines between digital output and input pins. Analog connections are shown as thick lines between analog output and input pins. Reference connections appear as thin lines between parameter array output and input pins. I assume you are referring to reference connections. How can references between blocks be configured using [product_name]?

Is it possible to read values from Modbus and use them to change the Off parameter of the Up/Down counter, but only if a certain condition is satisfied? If the Off parameter is important (shouldn't be altered unless Modbus is available or the process is at a specific stage), do you consider changing it via Modbus TCP a standard approach, or are there potential reliability issues? You can read values from Modbus with a [product_name] [version_no] to modify the OFF parameter. If you introduce a condition for this change, what should the OFF parameter be when the condition isn't met?
This is the third discussion regarding how to change the OFF parameter of an UP/DOWN counter. Shouldn't you share your overall concept with the group?

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to update the OFF parameter of an Up/Down counter in [product_name] dynamically using Modbus values, but only under specific conditions. There is discussion about whether this approach is considered best practice and reliable, especially when using [product_name] [version_no]. Questions are raised about the default value of the OFF parameter if the condition isn't met, and whether altering this parameter via Modbus is typically considered robust or problematic.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to reliably change the OFF parameter of the Up/Down counter through Modbus only when defined criteria are met, and anticipates standardized and dependable support for such dynamic control functions within [product_name].
